page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highmem-30 is a memory-dense virtual machine powered by the AMD EPYC 9B14 processor based on the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 30 dedicated vCPUs spanning 15 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU configuration features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside instruction set support for AVX-512 extensions including VNNI and BF16, as well as hardware cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI.

The instance is equipped with 240.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation that aligns with memory-intensive compute profiles. It does not include local storage or bundled GPU accelerators, requiring persistence and secondary storage to be attached remotely via network block volumes. In memory benchmarks, the system achieved a strong PassMark memory score of 2793.86, though uncached large-block memory write throughput measured at 24.31 GB/sec, reflecting a lower-tier result for sequential write-heavy access patterns.

Computational evaluations demonstrate balanced processing capability, marked by a top-quartile stress-ng single-core score of 2866.78 and a middle-tier multi-core score of 43062.67. Synthetic workloads registered 14454.0 on Geekbench multi-core and 41450.78 on PassMark CPU tests. In targeted evaluation suites, the instance showed solid efficiency in text processing and small-scale language model generation, reaching 309.23 tokens per second on a 135M parameter model, but performance dropped to 7.44 tokens per second during prompt ingestion for large 70B parameter models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c3d-highmem-30 offers substantial memory capacity relative to core count without the overhead of dedicated accelerator hardware. It is best suited for memory-bound relational databases, in-memory caching platforms such as Redis, large batch ETL jobs, and data analytics pipelines that do not depend on high-throughput local disk storage.
